title: Tap at its boom and the move into Hollywood musicals
summary: Green and the interviewers say tap was booming in the late 1930s worldwide and entering sound musicals; Green names acrobatic teams like Jack De-Rant.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Wasn't tap dancing at this point starting to diminish? Weren't the jobs lessening and lessening? This was what period? What time period?
Well, the time period was -- there was pictures, those -- "The March of Time" --
Are you talking about the '40's?
Well, it was approaching the '40's. It was right on the '40's.
It was actually in the late '30's.
Yeah, late '30's, that's it.
Now, was tap dancing at a boom or was it starting to diminish?
No, it was at a boom, yes. It was definitely at a boom.
I think throughout the world, I think they were picking it up in Europe. People were beginning to -- children, everybody wanted to do tap dancing classes. That's --
I don't know if that would be because of theater or films or (unintelligible) movies --
Were movies starting to incorporate tap dancing at this time as well?

That's right. That's where they went -- when they got to Hollywood -- see, because this -- these musicals were coming into the public's attention at that time. New shows and new styles of shows. The musical was it because it was all performing -- singing, dancing --
Wouldn't that be something to do with the development of sound with movies -- what year was that sound--
That's right.
Silent movies, then sound came about.
Uh-huh.
Who were some of the tap dancers that were on this -- on the circuit, the big band circuit? What were some of the other groups? What singles?
Well, there was the Mayo Brothers, the Dunhills. Some tall, tall guy -- what was his name? But he could really dance -- oh, yeah, Durant -- Jack De-Rant and his partner, you see.
What sort of style did they do?
Aero.
What's that?
Well, that's -- you could call it
precision or acrobatic, you see -- or contortion, see. But it was done to jazz, you see.
